content: 1. The canonical form of a full page name is displayed prominently as the page header. For example, the canonical form of this page is Help:Page_name, where underscores replace spaces in the URL. Alternative names for this page include help:page name, help:Page name, Help:page name, and Help:Page name, but not Help:Page Name. These variations depend on the project settings. 2. The terms full page name and full pagename include the namespace prefix, while page name and pagename can be ambiguous for pages outside the main namespace. To avoid confusion, it is recommended to use full pagename or pagename without namespace prefix. 3. Certain characters are prohibited in page titles. These include non-printable characters with values 0 through 31, the delete character (127), and characters like `{`, `}`, `|`, and `,` due to their special meanings in Wikipedia's syntax. For example, the `]` character points to the current year (2023) rather than a page named {{CURRENTYEAR}}. By default, the `+` character is also disallowed but can be enabled via the `$wgLegalTitleChars` configuration in `LocalSettings.php`. 4. A forward slash (`/`) in a page name may provide special functionality depending on the namespace and settings, such as enabling the subpage feature. 5. The first part of a page name cannot coincide with a project-independent namespace prefix that is automatically converted to another one. For instance, Project: A-Kon is not allowed on Wikipedia. However, a page name can coincide with a namespace prefix that is not converted, such as Wikipedia: The Big Adventure. In such cases, the page may end up in the wrong namespace, which can complicate searches or page listings. 6. Page names cannot begin with prefixes used to refer to other projects (e.g., en:) or pseudo-namespaces like Media: and Special:. For example, an article titled Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo. cannot use that exact name because it conflicts with the Q: prefix used in Wikiquote. 7. The maximum length of a page name is 255 bytes, excluding the namespace prefix. Non-ASCII characters may occupy up to four bytes in UTF-8 encoding, so the actual number of characters allowed depends on the language used. 8. In page names, spaces are equivalent to underscores. While spaces are displayed in the page title, underscores appear in the URL. For example, Page name is displayed as such, but the URL will show Page_name. 9. The case sensitivity of page names varies. Namespace prefixes are case-insensitive, but the first character of the page name (after the namespace prefix) may or may not be case-sensitive depending on the project. For example, on Wikimedia projects, the first character is generally case-insensitive, except in Wiktionaries. 10. The file name extension of an image is case-sensitive. For instance, image:Stop_sign_us.jpg and image:Stop_sign_us.JPG are treated as distinct files. 11. Spaces and underscores at the start or end of a full page name, or around a namespace prefix, are ignored. Duplicate consecutive spaces are also ignored. However, spaces before or after a normal colon are significant and can differentiate page names. 12. A page name cannot include encoded characters like %41 because they are automatically converted to their corresponding characters (e.g., %41 becomes A). This means distinct pages with names like %C3%80 and À cannot coexist. 13. The canonical form of a page name is used in inclusion tags for non-existent pages. For example, {{qwsazx}} and {{:qwsazx}} both resolve to Template:Qwsazx. However, interwiki links and links to other projects do not display the canonical form in hover text or the status bar. 14. There is no standalone feature to convert spaces to underscores or special characters to escape codes. However, the `localurl` and `PAGENAMEE` variables can perform these conversions in combination with other functions. For example, `{{PAGENAME}}` outputs Page name, while `{{PAGENAMEE}}` outputs Page_name. These variables are useful for constructing URLs or linking to pages programmatically. 15. When using `localurl`, `{{PAGENAME}}` should be used in the first part of the URL, while `{{PAGENAMEE}}` should be used in the second part. Incorrect usage can result in broken links, especially when special characters are involved.
